Raw inputs: Compustat annual fundamentals and annualized/as-of-December firm information for ROA, CFROA, RNOA, expenditures, accrual, market/book measures, equity issuance, BM ranking and low-BM cohort/industry medians.; Quarterly Compustat history for the prior-four-year ROA and year-over-year sales-growth variances (G4/G5), requiring at least six quarters; when these data are missing the paper codes the signals zero rather than dropping the observation.. Construct GSCORE as G1 + G2 + G3 + G4 + G5 + G6 + G7 + G8. Source definition: Additive index equal to the sum of the eight binary growth-fundamental signals G1–G8. Each signal defaults to 0 and equals 1 when its stated criterion is met: G1, ROA above the contemporaneous median for low-BM firms in the same two-digit SIC industry; G2, cash-flow ROA above that median; G3, cash-flow ROA above ROA; G4, quarterly ROA variance over the prior four years below that median; G5, variance of quarterly year-over-year sales growth, comparing Q0 with Q−4, over the prior four years below that median; G6–G8, respectively, R&D, capital-expenditure and advertising intensity above their corresponding medians. The intensity measures use beginning assets as denominator. G4 and G5 use quarterly data and require at least six quarters; when the required quarterly data are missing, the signals are coded zero rather than dropping the observation. Industry medians are at the two-digit SIC level within low-BM firms.. Exact current-vintage field-to-paper mapping limitations are recorded on the linked routes and in review notes.

implementation_issues.description: Table 7 labels the regressor BM and defines it as the book-to-market ratio at formation, while Section 4.4 calls the control LBM and defines it as log(BM). The selected full-control equation therefore has an unresolved variable definition.
The article reports annual cross-sectional regressions but does not state the regression estimator or standard-error/covariance correction in the selected table.

GSCORE requires eight indicator constructions, prior-year low-BM cutoffs, contemporaneous two-digit SIC low-BM industry medians, quarterly-history minimums, and default-zero coding when quarterly histories are missing; these steps require substantial panel construction.

MOM, SRET1 and capitalization-decile adjustment require CRSP return-window construction and the paper's stated Shumway delisting adjustment; benchmark breakpoints/portfolio composition are not fully specified.

review_notes: Table 7 uses annual cross-sectional full-control regressions for the low-BM firm-year sample (1979–2001). Out-of-sample and high-BM tests are not added.

The paper's sample selection starts with Compustat 1978–2001, uses prior-year BM cutoffs, and calculates G4/G5 from trailing four-year quarterly data with a six-quarter minimum; missing G4/G5 histories are coded zero.
The paper reports 21,253 Table 7 observations in aggregate across the annual fits, distinct from nearby descriptive/correlation counts; no sample-size inference is made from the count difference.

evidence.quote: Firm level returns are computed as the buy-and-hold returns for the 12-month and 24-month period starting on the 1st of May of the year after portfolio formation
The returns are size-adjusted by subtracting the returns in the same period for the same capitalization decile as the firm on CRSP.

SRET1 and SRET12 are the size-adjusted buy-and-hold returns respectively, for 1-year and 2-year periods starting May 1st for the year after portfolio formation. When a firm delists, delisting returns are used as in Shumway (1997).
GSCORE is the sum of eight fundamental signals, G1:G8, tailored for growth firms. G1:G8 have a default value of 0 and equal 1 if the following criteria are met respectively.
I define the first growth signal, G1, to equal 1 if a firm’s ROA is greater than the contemporaneous median ROA for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise.
ROA, defined as the ratio of net income before extraordinary items scaled by average total assets.
I define the second growth signal, G2, to equal 1 if a firm’s cash flow ROA exceeds the contemporaneous median for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise.
G3 is defined to equal if a firm’s cash flow from operations exceeds net income and 0 otherwise.
G4 is defined to equal 1 if a firm’s earnings variability is less than the contemporaneous median for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise.
G5 is defined to equal 1 it a firm’s sale growth variability is less than the contemporaneous median for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise.

G6, G7 and G8 are defined to equal 1 if a firm’s R&D, capital expenditure and advertising intensity respectively, are greater than the contemporaneous medians of the corresponding variables for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise. The intensity of R&D, capital expenditure and advertising are measured by deflating these variables by beginning assets.

The two signals related to naı ̈ve extrapolation, i.e. earnings variability and sales growth variability (G4,G5) are generated from quarterly financials of the past 4 years, with the constraint that at least six quarters information be available.
If these data are missing, the observations are not deleted, but the signals are coded as zeroes.
Industry medians are calculated at the two-digit SIC level within low BM firms.
I measure growth variability as the variance of a firm’s year over year sales growth (Q0 compared to Q)4) over the past 4 years using quarterly information.
SIZE is measured as log of market capitalization.
BM is the BM ratio at the time of portfolio formation.
LBM – log of the BM ratio
MOM – size-adjusted buy-and-hold return for the 6 month period prior to portfolio formation
MOM is the buy and old return for the 6 month period before portfolio formation.
ACCR is a dummy that equals 1 if net income exceeds cash from operations.
EQ_OFF is a dummy that equals 1 if a film issued equity in the year prior to portfolio formation.
The t-statistics are adjusted for auto-correlation using the method outlined in Bernard (1995).
